::: {#exm-paradigms}
#### Two views of a success probability

Suppose 55 of 91 independent trials succeed.
A frequentist treats the success probability $\prob$ as a fixed number,
estimates it by $\hprob = 55/91 \approx 0.60$,
and describes uncertainty by how much $\hprob$ would vary
over repeated sets of 91 trials,
for example with a confidence interval.
A Bayesian gives $\prob$ a probability distribution before seeing the trials,
such as the uniform distribution on $(0, 1)$,
and describes uncertainty by the distribution of $\prob$ given the 55 successes.
:::
